_meta.source: NayaCore.exe string tables (NayaFlow's protocol binary, not the Electron app)
_meta.why: This is the vocabulary the layer sitting directly on the wire uses, so it is a better source than the app-side naya-gesture-enum.json. It is still a VOCABULARY: it says what NayaCore can name, not what the firmware implements. LED brightness, the Track hold and mouse-on-key are all named somewhere and unbacked by hardware.
_meta.order: As they appear in the binary. Whether that order maps to config field indices is untested -- see docs/module-field-map.md.

key_behavior_types_are_indexed_by_record.finding: The list index IS the record type byte. Verified against eight types derived independently from captures: bluetooth=0x00, key_press=0x01, mod_tap=0x03, mo=0x05, none=0x07, to_layer=0x0c, toggle_layer=0x0d, trans=0x0e.

consequences.0x02: macro -- the key record that references a macro. Param shape untested; the layer behaviours at 0x05/0x0c/0x0d all take a u32 LE index, so a macro index is the first thing to try.
consequences.0x08: outputs (ZMK &out, USB/BLE selection). We call 0x08 LAYER_SW in remap.py -- that name is probably WRONG and should be checked before it misleads someone.
consequences.0x0f: mouse. We call this TWO_WORD, which is a format name we invented; semantically a KEY position takes the same two-word record a module gesture does. This answers the Phase 4 blocker -- mouse on a key was 'we know the module form but not what a key takes'.

key_behavior_types_are_indexed_by_record.caveat: A record type existing does not mean the firmware implements it. NayaCore itself writes NONE for a macro binding (measured 2026-09-07), so 0x02 is a name in a table, not a demonstrated behaviour. Test before building.
